issues.problem: Miscount. The footer "Quick Menu" has six links (Home/index.html, About Us/about.html, Services/services.html, Special Offers/special-offers.html, Contact Us/contact.html, Book Online/booking.html) and every one of them returns the WordPress 404 page (verified by fetching all six root .html paths: about.html, index.html, services.html, special-offers.html, contact.html, booking.html). The header logo link also points at index.html.
issues.fix: Change to "six footer links are dead (home, about, services, special offers, contact and booking)" or "all six footer-menu links"; the analysis.json count needs the same correction.

issues.claim: For-the-founder notes: "No booking volume, menu price, headcount or review count is published"
issues.problem: Overstated. Review counts are publicly visible: Bing's card for the address shows a Yelp listing at 4.0/5 from 4 reviews, and the salon's Facebook page shows "100% recommend (11 reviews)" (both already recorded in profile.json). Only Google's review count is hidden in the signed-out Maps view.
issues.fix: Say "no menu prices, booking volumes or headcount are published, and Google's review count is not visible in the signed-out view".

issues.claim: Section 2: "two ways in — the phone and a callback-only request form"
issues.problem: Incomplete. /contact-us/ also carries a general "Send a Message" form (Contact Form 7), so a visitor has a third way to send an enquiry; the researcher's own profile notes this second form.
issues.fix: Say "for bookings, two ways in — the phone and a callback-only request form" (and note the general contact form on /contact-us/).

issues.problem: Minor arithmetic inconsistency: 0.2 hrs/week x 52 weeks = 10.4 hours, so the low end is $225.89 at $21.72/hr, not $217.20 (that figure uses a flat 10 hours). The error understates, so it is safe, but the two endpoints imply different hour counts.
issues.fix: Use 10.4 hours -> about $226–$565, or state the assumption as "0.2–0.5 hours a week, i.e. roughly 10–26 hours a year".

issues.claim: Method framing of the dollar ranges (1.25x benefits on saved staff hours; "100% share automated")
issues.problem: Transparently labelled as assumptions, but loading 25% benefits onto saved hours and assuming 100% automation of the estimated time presents a labour-cost equivalent rather than cash the salon would keep; a reader could read it as realisable savings.
issues.fix: Keep the arithmetic but relabel as "labour-cost equivalent of about $X, if the time is fully automated and hours are actually cut" — one clause is enough.
